physics.energy-resources-describe-kb.000.all: Gas burned to heat water into high-pressure steam; steam turns turbine; turbine turns generator producing electricity

physics.energy-resources-explain-kb.0004.all: Short start-up time; can be switched on/increase output quickly to match demand

physics.energy-resources-extended-kb.001.a: Water stored high behind dam (GPE); released, flows down gaining KE; turns turbines which drive generators
physics.energy-resources-extended-kb.001.b: Plan: coal - reliable, constant output, controllable, cheap fuel, but CO2 (global warming), SO2 (acid rain), non-renewable. Wind - renewable, no emissions/fuel cost, but unreliable (depends on wind), lower output per turbine so needs large area, visual/noise. Conclusion with justification e.g. wind plus backup.

physics.energy-resources-recall-kb.0011.c: No CO2 emissions / lots of energy from small mass of fuel / reliable

physics.energy-thermal-describe-kb.0005.a: Hot end particles vibrate more; pass vibrations to neighbours via collisions; free electrons gain KE and move through metal transferring energy quickly
physics.energy-thermal-describe-kb.0005.b: Land heats faster than sea; air above land warms, expands, less dense, rises; cooler denser air from sea moves in to replace it

physics.energy-thermal-explain-kb.0005.all: Metal is a better conductor; transfers energy away from hand faster so hand cools quickly

physics.energy-thermal-extended-kb.0010.a: Air near heater warms, expands, becomes less dense and rises; cools at ceiling/far side, becomes denser and sinks; returns to heater - circulating current
physics.energy-thermal-extended-kb.0010.b: Plan: conduction - loft insulation/cavity wall foam trap air (poor conductor), double glazing air/vacuum gap. Convection - foam in cavity stops air circulating, draught excluders, double glazing narrow gap. Radiation - shiny foil behind radiators/in loft reflects IR back, light-coloured surfaces emit less.

physics.energy-transfers-describe-kb.001.a: Gravitational potential store decreases; kinetic store increases (some to thermal via air resistance)
physics.energy-transfers-describe-kb.001.b: Electrical work by current; increases thermal store of water (some wasted to surroundings/sound)
physics.energy-transfers-describe-kb.001.c: Chemical store of fuel; transferred by combustion to thermal and kinetic store of car; wasted as thermal to surroundings and sound

physics.energy-transfers-recall-kb.0008.a: kinetic, gravitational potential (chemical, thermal, elastic, nuclear, magnetic, electrostatic)
physics.energy-transfers-recall-kb.0008.b: Transferred to surroundings as thermal energy (dissipated, heats surroundings)

physics.energy-work-explain-kb.0008.a: Same work done (same weight, same height); in less time so power = work/time is greater
physics.energy-work-explain-kb.0008.b: KE = 1/2 m v^2 so doubling speed quadruples KE; braking force does work = F x d; so braking distance about four times

physics.energy-work-recall-kb.0006.a: GPE = m x g x h

physics.forces-elasticity-explain-kb.001.a: Straight line through origin; extension directly proportional to force
physics.forces-elasticity-explain-kb.001.b: Graph curves / not straight; extension not proportional to force
physics.forces-elasticity-explain-kb.001.c: Avoid parallax error; reading would be too high/low, more accurate

physics.forces-elasticity-recall-kb.0007.a: Object returns to original shape/length when force removed

physics.forces-forces-describe-kb.0006.a: At start weight only, air resistance zero; as speed increases air resistance increases, resultant force decreases; at terminal velocity air resistance equals weight, resultant zero
physics.forces-forces-describe-kb.0006.b: Same direction add; opposite directions subtract; direction of larger force
physics.forces-forces-describe-kb.0006.c: Friction acts opposite to motion; reduces resultant force/acceleration, heats surfaces, need push = friction for constant speed

physics.forces-forces-explain-kb.0003.all: Less friction between tyres and road; smaller braking force/deceleration so greater braking distance

physics.forces-forces-extended-kb.0001.all: Plan: starts weight only, accelerates at 10 m/s^2; speed up, drag up, resultant & acceleration fall; drag = weight terminal velocity; parachute opens: drag > weight, decelerates; drag falls as slows until equal weight, new lower terminal velocity; lands at low speed.

physics.forces-forces-recall-kb.0005.b: Vector has magnitude and direction, scalar magnitude only

physics.forces-moments-explain-kb.0002.all: Load produces clockwise moment about tower; counterweight produces anticlockwise moment; balances moments so crane doesn't topple/centre of gravity over base

physics.forces-moments-mcq-kb.0014.c: the same force gives a larger moment

physics.forces-moments-recall-kb.0006.a: For an object in equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments about a pivot = sum of anticlockwise moments
physics.forces-moments-recall-kb.0006.b: Point through which the weight appears to act

physics.forces-momentum-explain-kb.0014.a: Increases time to stop ball; same momentum change so smaller force (F = change in momentum / time)
physics.forces-momentum-explain-kb.0014.b: Rocket exerts downward force on gas; gas exerts equal and opposite upward force on rocket (N3) / momentum conserved

physics.forces-momentum-mcq-kb.0007.all: has a direction as well as a size

physics.forces-momentum-recall-kb.0014.a: Total momentum before = total momentum after; provided no external forces act
